- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing short-term price momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 60+), model overreacts with excessive overshoot in the immediate following days.
- Model shows weak mean reversion — fails to pull prices back toward historical averages after peaks.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the final 5–10 days, underestimating late-period price rebounds.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias across all horizons, suggesting a structural underestimation of price volatility or demand shocks.
- Adjust forecasts upward by 2–5% for the first 5 days, and by 3–7% for the last 5 days to correct for lag and horizon bias.
- Avoid overreacting to recent spikes — reduce forecast overshoot by 10–20% in the immediate aftermath of price surges.
